title: Keys, Functional Dependencies & Minimal Canonical Cover
subtitle: Super Keys, Candidate Keys, Armstrong's Axioms & Attribute Closure Solvers
mentalModel: Functional dependencies define business invariants and data constraints between attributes. Attribute Closure (X)⁺ calculates the full reachability of attribute sets under Armstrong's Axioms, enabling automatic detection of Candidate Keys and minimal canonical covers.

failureModes: Extraneous attribute bloat: Defining composite candidate keys with redundant attributes (Super Keys) increases index tree height and reduces write throughput.
Redundant dependency cycles: Non-minimal FD sets cause redundant constraint verification checks inside database transaction engines.
Partial key violations: Failing to enforce that all non-prime attributes depend on full Candidate Keys causes update and deletion anomalies in production.

tradeOffs.aspect: Synthetic Surrogate Key (UUID/BigInt AUTO_INCREMENT) vs Natural Composite Key
tradeOffs.optionA: Surrogate Key: Fixed 8-byte integer size, fast B+ Tree clustered indexing, immune to business attribute mutations.
tradeOffs.optionB: Natural Key: Enforces domain uniqueness without secondary indexes, but larger key bytes reduce page branching factor.

tradeOffs.optionA: Full Closure Precomputation: Identifies all normal forms and candidate keys at compile time.
tradeOffs.optionB: On-demand Closure: Evaluates single dependency validity dynamically.

theoryData.productionScenario: A healthcare provider table PatientVisits(patient_id, doctor_id, clinic_id, appointment_time, doctor_specialty) experienced data corruption because doctor_specialty depended only on doctor_id (Partial Dependency). Decomposing into Doctors(doctor_id, doctor_specialty) and Appointments(patient_id, doctor_id, clinic_id, appointment_time) eliminated 100,000 duplicate specialty updates per day.

interviewQA.question: What is the difference between a Prime Attribute and a Non-Prime Attribute?
interviewQA.answer: A Prime Attribute is any attribute that is a member of AT LEAST ONE candidate key for the relation. A Non-Prime Attribute does not belong to any candidate key.

interviewQA.question: What is a Minimal Canonical Cover (Fc) of a set of functional dependencies?
interviewQA.answer: A Canonical Cover Fc is an equivalent minimal set of FDs such that: 1. Every right-hand side is a single attribute. 2. No dependency contains extraneous left-hand side attributes. 3. No dependency in Fc is redundant.

quizData.question: If attribute set X has closure (X)⁺ containing all attributes of relation R, what is X guaranteed to be?
quizData.explanation: Any attribute set whose closure covers all relation attributes is a Super Key (and a Candidate Key if it is minimal).

quizData.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Armstrong's primary axioms?
quizData.explanation: The 3 fundamental Armstrong's Axioms are Reflexivity, Augmentation, and Transitivity. Composition/Union are derived secondary rules.
